slides.say: A B C D is a parallelogram. Given: A B is ten centimeters, B C is fourteen centimeters, and angle A B C is one hundred fifty degrees. What is the area of the parallelogram, in square centimeters?
at: A B C D is a parallelogram

slides.say: The area of a parallelogram is base times height. The base B C is fourteen, so we need the height to B C. [short pause] Angle B is obtuse, so first we need to see where that height falls.

[short pause] Here's the base, B C, fourteen. We drop the height from A, straight down to the line of B C. Because angle B is obtuse, A is to the left of B, so the height falls outside the parallelogram.
So we start at B and extend C B beyond B. Then we drop the height from A to that line, and call its foot H.
Angle A B H and angle A B C sit together on one straight line, so angle A B H is one hundred eighty minus one hundred fifty, which is thirty.
at: so angle A B H is

slides.say: Triangle A B H has a right angle and a thirty degree angle, so it's a gold triangle, thirty, sixty, ninety. A B is its hypotenuse, ten. The height A H is across from the thirty, so it's the short leg, and the short leg is half the hypotenuse. Half of ten is five.
The area is base times height, fourteen times five, seventy. Choice number three is our answer.
at: Choice number three is our answer

slides.say: So when you see a thirty degree angle, or a hundred fifty next to it, the height is half the slanted side. And the other choices are traps. A hundred forty is fourteen times ten, the slanted side instead of the height. Seventy root three uses the long leg instead of the short one. And thirty-five divides by two, which is the triangle formula. [pause] Okay. I'll see you in the next question.
